I ran the `/code-conventions --review-pr` checklist on `git diff a8ca1696a...HEAD` (the Express → Fastify migration, 122 files). I considered all 60 rules and marked them checked in the generated checklist, which is gitignored and untracked. No tracked files were changed, and no tests or `gh` commands were run.

**Rules that applied:** CHANGE-01, CHANGE-02, CHANGE-04, PR-01, PR-02, MOD-04, NAME-01, REUSE-01, STYLE-01, TYPE-06, AUTH-01, ROUTE-01, CONFIG-02, CONFIG-04, CONFIG-05, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-07, TEST-09, LOG-01, LOG-04, SEC-02, RESILIENCE-01. The rest didn't touch this diff (DB, cache, DTO, space-membership rules and so on).

**Zoom used:** Level 1 for MOD-04, which confirmed the "don't export what no other module uses" learning (RL-20251216-002). No Level 2 lookups.

**License headers:** every `.ts` file this PR touches has the SPDX header. The only one missing is the deleted `src/routes/common/decorators/utils.ts`.

## Findings

| # | Rule | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CONFIG-04 | `package.json:52-53` | `@fastify/cookie` (`^11.0.2`) and `@fastify/static` (`^9.1.3`) are new runtime dependencies with caret ranges. The rule says to pin exactly, and the dependency this PR replaced (`@nestjs/platform-express`) was pinned. |
| 2 | PR-02 / CONFIG-05 | `src/config/entities/configuration.ts:407-417`, `.env.sample.json:682` | The comments and env descriptions still describe Express behaviour: body-parser, the `bytes` library, Express `trust proxy`, and links to expressjs.com. The values now feed the Fastify `bodyLimit`/`trustProxy` options and a custom parser, so the docs no longer match what runs. Keeping the `EXPRESS_*` env names is fine under CHANGE-04; only the wording is stale. |
| 3 | MOD-04 | `src/app.provider.ts:34`, `src/app.provider.ts:38` | `parseTrustProxy` and `parseBodyLimit` are exported, but nothing outside `app.provider.ts` imports them, not even a test. They should stay module-local unless a spec gets added (see #7). |
| 4 | CHANGE-01 / STYLE-01 | `src/routes/common/http/http-request.utils.ts:7-25`, `:40-41`, `:53-54` | `RequestLike` and its helpers keep Express-only fallbacks: `header()`, `get()`, `route.path`, `path`, `originalUrl`. After the migration, `FastifyRequest` never reaches these branches, so they're dead code. The only remaining non-Fastify caller is `NotFoundLoggerMiddleware`, and it only needs `originalUrl`/`url`/`headers`. |
| 5 | TEST-07 / TEST-09 | `src/routes/common/http/http-request.utils.spec.ts:15-17` | The `getRouteUrl` spec only mocks the Express-style `request.get()`. The path production actually uses (reading from `request.headers`, and the `host`/`hostname` fallbacks) has no test. The spec passes because of the legacy branch in #4. |
| 6 | LOG-01 | `src/routes/common/http/http-request.utils.ts:67-73` | When headers are missing, `getRouteUrl` quietly falls back to `'http'` and `'localhost'`. Pagination and route URLs would then point to `http://localhost/...` instead of failing or logging. The rule says default-fallback paths must not return a plausible-looking wrong value. |
| 7 | TEST-02 / TEST-09 | `src/app.provider.ts:38-56` | `parseBodyLimit` is a new hand-written parser (units, decimals, whitespace, a throw on invalid input) that replaces body-parser's parsing. Its only coverage is one integration test using a bare byte count (`'8'`). `kb`/`mb`, decimals, uppercase input, the invalid-input throw and the `'1mb'` default all belong in a unit spec. `parseTrustProxy`'s numeric-versus-list branch also has no direct test. |
| 8 | NAME-01 | `src/modules/auth/oidc/routes/oidc-auth.controller.ts:110`, `src/modules/auth/oidc/routes/oidc-auth.service.ts:147` | The same service now returns `maxAge` in seconds (`getSecondsUntil`) but `stateMaxAge` still in milliseconds. The controller converts with an inline `Math.floor(stateMaxAge / 1_000)`. Two cookie max-age fields from one service in different units, with nothing in the names to say so, invites a unit bug. Return seconds from the service, or name the field `stateMaxAgeMs`. |
| 9 | REUSE-01 | `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-cookie.utils.ts:3-9` | `CookieOptions` is written by hand to replace Express's type. `@fastify/cookie` (the new dependency) already exports `CookieSerializeOptions`, which is what `res.setCookie`/`clearCookie` accept. A local copy can drift from it. |
| 10 | TYPE-06 | `src/__tests__/test-app.provider.ts:18-20`, `src/app.provider.ts:128-129` | `createTestApplication` casts `as NestFastifyApplication` when the generic `createNestApplication<NestFastifyApplication>(...)` would do, and `TestAppProvider.provide` already uses the generic form. `configureCookies` casts `(app as NestFastifyApplication)` because `DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION` is still typed as `INestApplication`. Typing the configuration array as `NestFastifyApplication` would remove the cast. |
| 11 | CHANGE-02 (low) | `src/app.provider.ts:2`, `src/middleware/not-found-logger.middleware.ts:2`, `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-cookie.utils.ts:2`, `src/modules/hooks/routes/hooks.controller.integration.spec.ts:2`, `src/modules/owners/routes/__tests__/get-safes-by-owner.e2e-spec.ts:2`, `src/modules/swaps/domain/swaps.repository.e2e-spec.ts:2` | A blank line was inserted after the SPDX header in files that didn't have one before. It's unrelated formatting churn; the repo is mixed (482 of 1,775 files have the blank line). |
| 12 | STYLE-01 (low) | `src/app.provider.spec.ts:71`, `src/app.provider.spec.ts:91` | Comments that explained the trust-proxy assertions were deleted, though the behaviour they described is unchanged under Fastify. |

**Open questions (no rule covers these):**
- About 21 source files import types from `'fastify'`, but `fastify` isn't a direct dependency; it comes in through `@nestjs/platform-fastify`. The rules don't say whether packages you import from must be declared directly.
- `main.ts:15` reads the raw `configuration()` before the app starts, so the Fastify adapter is built before `ConfigurationService` validation runs. The code comment explains why. It's acceptable under CONFIG-02 only because `parseBodyLimit` throws at startup on bad input.

**Changes made:** none (review only). No unresolved checklist items beyond the findings above.
